findings.title: Unexpected exceptions skip the report the docstring promises
findings.description: The module docstring says that on any failure "the report is still written". `run_steps` catches only `StepFailed` and `CalledProcessError`, and `main()` has no `try/finally` around it. Other exceptions escape before `report.write_text` at line 312. Realistic cases: `read_text()` on a missing `backup-health.log` (line 224), `CRON_FILE.read_text()` at line 95, `IndexError` on an empty `base.log` (line 181), and `conf_sums()` at `scripts/cutover_227_host.py:82`, where `next(...)` has no default and raises `StopIteration` if `17/main` is missing from `pg_lsclusters`. The run then fails with a traceback and no audit file. Either wrap the step runner so every exception records a FAIL step and still writes the report, or fix the docstring.

findings.title: A same-day re-run overwrites the failure report
findings.description: The report is named `<date>-227-cutover.md`, so a second run on the same day replaces the first run's report. The documented recovery is "fix the cause, re-run", which is exactly when the failed run's evidence gets lost. The sibling scripts use timestamps: `scripts/provision_tick_cluster.sh:112` and `cutover_921`'s `%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ`. Use a timestamped name.

findings.title: The report is written into a git-tracked directory without the credential scan the sibling script applies
findings.description: `provision_tick_cluster.sh:351-353` runs `log_scrub` before it copies its log into `project-documents/user/notes/`. The cutover records provision's full output (`step_provision`, via `record()` at `scripts/cutover_227_host.py:109-114`) and the setup-backup and health output, then writes them to the same directory with no scrub. The likelihood is low, since the provision script avoids printing secrets, but the rule the sibling enforces is not applied here. Reuse `log_scrub` on the report before writing it.

findings.title: `b2_lifecycle.sh` folds rclone's stderr into the JSON it parses
findings.description: `RULES=$(... rclone backend lifecycle ... 2>&1)` merges every stderr line into the rule list. Any log line rclone writes on a successful run then makes `jq` fail. That is reported as `MISSING <cluster> lifecycle-read`, which setup-backup tallies as not-OK, so the check fails with the rules readable. This is probably a real risk: setup-backup runs as root under sudo, where rclone may have no config file and would print a "config file not found" notice. I could not run rclone here to confirm the exact output. Capture stdout alone, and send stderr to a separate variable that is only shown on failure.

findings.title: The same values are scattered across cutover, setup-backup, and the cron scripts
findings.description:
- `CHECK_ALLOWED` and `APPLY_ALLOWED` hard-code `17/tick`, `cron\.d`, and the item labels `arm-file` and `PENDING RESTART`, all of which match setup-backup's output text. Renaming an item in setup-backup breaks the cutover silently.
- `ARM_FILE` is defined here (line 69) and again in `deploy/setup-backup.sh:80`.
- `PUSH_MIN_AGE` exists in three places: `PUSH_MIN_AGE_S = 120` (line 68), `PUSH_MIN_AGE_SEC=120` in `scripts/cron_weekly_backup.sh:54`, and `MIN_AGE=2m` in `scripts/sync_wal_offsite.sh:34`.
- `CRON_FILE`, `TICK_UNIT`, `HOST_BACKUP_ROOT`, and `RCLONE_REMOTE` are each defined in Python and again in setup-backup.sh.
- `strip_new_args` (`scripts/cutover_227_helpers.py:87`) hard-codes `127.0.0.1`, which is also in `deploy/backup-clusters.conf:20`.

Each value should have one definition that the others read.

findings.title: A vacuous assertion in the cutover tests
findings.description: `all("manta " not in c.split("/")[0] for c in commands.values())` always passes. `commands` values are the command strings after the user field, and they start with `/home/...`, so `split("/")[0]` is always `""`. The assertion is meant to catch a user name leaking into the command, and it cannot fail. Delete it, or check `c` directly.

findings.title: The REPLICATION grant branch is never executed by any test
findings.description: The new `\if :{?with_replication}` block issues `ALTER ROLE ... REPLICATION`, a powerful role attribute. `test/tick_support/database.py` runs the roles file without `with_replication` (no match for "replication" in that directory), so the grant path never runs. The only coverage is `test/unit/test_provision_tick_lib.py:255-258`, which checks that the `ALTER` text appears before `\else`. That passes even if the grant is moved outside the guard. Add an integration case that runs the file with `-v with_replication=1` and asserts `rolreplication` for `tick_migrate` and its absence when the variable is not passed.

findings.title: `test_setup_backup.py` has grown to 1072 lines
findings.description: This diff adds roughly 250 lines to a file that already exceeded the ~300-line guideline. Split it by subject: argument parsing, the cluster table, render, and lifecycle.

findings.title: A no-op `replace` in a size assertion
findings.description: `assert "@" not in text.replace("@192", "")` is a no-op today, since no `@192` appears in the rendered output. It reads like a weakened check and should be removed or explained.

findings.title: The cutover script is 320 lines
findings.description: This is slightly over the ~300-line guideline. The step functions could move to their own module, which would also help the coverage gaps below.

findings.title: The `17/tick` step assumes the cluster already exists
findings.description: Setup-backup now exits if a table cluster is missing from `pg_lsclusters`, but the cutover runs `--check` at step 2 and provisions `17/tick` at step 3. This works on manta9000 because slice 226 created the cluster first. The step's expected text, "17/tick not yet set up", is wrong for a host where 226 never ran.

findings.title: `env_value` interpolates a path into a bash command string
findings.description: `cmd = f'. "{lib}"; env_value "$1" "$2"'` builds bash source from the library path. Pass the path as a positional argument instead.

findings.title: Dead references to the dropped proof database
findings.description: Provisioning no longer creates `trading_tick_proof` or writes `MT_PROOF_226_*`, but the 226 proof harness and `TICK_PROOF_DB_NAME` still target them. The slice doc says the proof database is intentionally gone, so the harness is dead and should be marked as historical.

findings.title: Several cutover steps and the failure path have no tests
findings.description: Tested: restart, weekly, production, health flags, and the step-runner stop. Not tested: `step_check`, `step_apply`, `step_provision`, `step_offsite` (including the WAL `--min-age` arithmetic), `main()`, and the unexpected-exception path from the first finding.

findings.title: Some new provisioning tests scan source text
findings.description: `test_only_trading_tick_is_created`, `test_parent_directories_755_data_directory_700`, and `test_roles_are_applied_with_replication` assert on how the script is spelled, not on what it does. The `hba_content` test runs the real function and is the better model.

findings.title: The advisory-lock query matches `pg_locks` encoding
findings.description: Both keys (`220_000_001` and `220_000_002`, from `src/manta_trading/data/tick/constants.py:172,240`) fit in 32 bits. For a single bigint advisory lock, `pg_locks` reports `classid=0`, `objid=key`, `objsubid=1`, so the query matches.

findings.title: The health and weekly output contracts match the scripts
findings.description: `FLAGS archive=N stale=M` matches `scripts/check_backup_health.sh:198`, and the cron wrapper puts it on one log line. `=== weekly backup done` matches both done lines in `scripts/cron_weekly_backup.sh:154,171`. The skip check uses the same `%Y%m%d` base directory naming as `cron_weekly_backup.sh:123`. The cutover creating the arm file at `cutover_227_tick_backup.py:188` follows TD7 in the slice design, so it is intended and not a finding.
